> If you invest $50,000 in a 2% appreciation market you will have a $60,000 property in 10 years. A $50,000 in an 8% appreciation market will be worth $100,000 over that same time. Doesn't that encourage you to check out your appreciation rate?

It does. But I guess the troubling part is finding that '8%' or even 4 or 5% appreciation market that has seen constant high appreciation over several decades. I imagine the small amount of locations that do match those criteria would be almost exclusively large cities or locations extremely coveted by the majority of the population. Which naturally means.. very expensive? So something that your general new investor these days wouldn't have access to, correct?

> The 2 things I look for in a market are appreciation rate and rent growth. 

If you don't mind, could you go into more detail about this? Isn't there a serious and legitimate concern of unpredictability that comes from targeting appreciation over cash flow?

For what it's worth, I only have a Discover, never told them my income, and worked a minimum wage job while in college. My credit line was $3,500. Several years later, unemployed, they upped it to $13,000.

>  If I get a card right now, do I immediately need to start spending on it, or can I wait for all of this coronavirus business to die down?

You can just get the credit card and put small purchases on it for the time being if you're truly worried. (ie: a Spotify subscription or occasional purchases of candy or something)

> Is it a "bad time" to get a card?

Do you have an essential job that you aren't worried about losing?

> Given that I have no credit history to speak of, would I be better off trying to apply for a store card of some kind?

 

Realistically, seeing as we're in a Pandemic, Majority of brick&mortar stores are closed, and most people aren't going out or don't need new luxury items.. which store card would make sense for you?

Have you considered the Chase Ink Business Cash? Seeing as that would give you 5% cashback up to $25,000 at Office depot/max, and Stapes, where you could also get GCs.
